it follows that the portion of living labour, unpaid and
congealed in surplus-value, must also be continually on the decrease compared
to the amount of value represented by the invested total capital. Since the
ratio of the mass of surplus-value to the value of the invested total capital
forms the rate of profit, this rate must constantly fall.
explanation: The Tendency of the Rate of Profit to Fall (TRPF): As technology advances, capitalists spend more on machinery (c) relative to human labor (v). Because only labor creates surplus value, profit rates tend to decline over time.
